verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own docs say that when a formula defines a bottle (prebuilt binary) matching your system, `brew install` downloads and installs it automatically, and building from source happens only when the user asks with `--build-from-source`. Casks also install upstream prebuilt binaries, and a Trail of Bits auditor independently notes that Homebrew serves its own binary builds. A community report says Linux prebuilt executables require the /home/linuxbrew prefix, which is a limitation rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of local download-cache reuse, and prebuilt-binary coverage for non-default prefixes on Linux.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install prebuilt binary packages from a cache instead of compiling from source

citations.quote: When the formula being installed defines a bottle matching your system, it will be downloaded and installed automatically when you run `brew install <formula>`.
Casks are package definitions that install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins.
the findings on Homebrew were not inconsistent with what I'd expect to find on any similarly sized userspace package manager that serves its own binary builds
